description: We are Space Minds! Our project, Field Shift, aims to help farmers in Uzbekistan adapt to climate change through innovative ideas and technology. We are passionate about science, agriculture, space and creating a better future. We are looking for creative, motivated and responsible teammates interested in technology, environmental science, data analysis and agriculture. Together, we can make a difference!
summary:
Our project, SpaceMind, is a website that helps farmers in Uzbekistan understand climate change and prepare for it.
The website has a map of Uzbekistan. Users can see the condition of plants, soil moisture and drought risk in each region. The website also gives advice about planting time, crop types and watering.
We use NASA data and show it in a simple way so everyone can understand it. Our website also has an analysis section and an AI assistant that can answer questions.
This project is important because water shortages and droughts are becoming serious problems in Uzbekistan. We want to help farmers save water and make better decisions for their farms.
details:
Our project is a website called SpaceMind Field Shift. It helps farmers in Uzbekistan understand climate risks before the season starts. We use free NASA satellite data and turn it into simple maps and advice. On the map, you click a region and see how healthy the plants are, how much water is in the soil, and how big the drought risk is. If you move the heat slider, you can see how the risk grows when it gets hotter. The site also has a farm game that lasts 30 weeks, a field planner, a quiz and an AI helper that answers questions about farming and climate. It works in English, Russian and Uzbek.

The website is free and works in any browser, even without internet. Farmers get simple answers: what to plant, when to plant and how much to water. They can practice in the game before making a real decision.

We want to help farmers adapt to climate change. About 90% of Uzbekistan’s water goes to agriculture, it became about 1.5 °C warmer since 1950, and the Aral Sea lost 88% of its area. By 2035, we want every farmer to see climate risks of their field early, save water and protect the harvest.

We used HTML, CSS and JavaScript to build the site, and SVG and Canvas for graphics. The AI helper on the site works through a Netlify Function (Node.js) connected to the Claude API. The site is hosted on Netlify. We used NASA data: MODIS and Landsat (plant health), SMAP (soil water), GPM (rain), ECOSTRESS (plant heat stress) and POWER (weather). We also used Claude, an AI assistant, to help us write the code. We did not need any special hardware.

Our idea is creative because we turned hard satellite science into something simple and fun, like a game, a quiz and a planner. The site reads text aloud, works offline and speaks three languages.

We thought about a few important things. The data must be honest, so we show the sources and say that the numbers for regions are model estimates. The language must be simple. The site must work with a slow internet and old phones. And we are a small school team, so we made a realistic project that can grow later with live NASA data and tests with real farmers.
